ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy set with standout China>Rider and historic Phil 6‑string debut
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a blazing China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition alongside strong renditions of Touch of Grey, Far From Me and Cassidy. Phil Lesh debuts his Alembic six‑string bass, adding fresh low‑end texture to the tight 1982 band sound. Several soundboard sources exist, with the Miller clean‑up recording offering the clearest listening experience.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Oakland Auditorium Arena is a vivid snapshot of the Dead in late‑'82: the band rides high on a set that mixes new material like Touch of Grey and Throwing Stones with classic early‑80s staples. Jerry Garcia’s lead work shines especially on “Eyes Of The World” and he “goes off” throughout, while Phil Lesh makes history by unveiling his Alembic six‑string bass for the first time, giving the low end a richer, more articulate voice. Brent Mydland’s keyboards weave subtle color under the jams, and the twin drummers keep a propulsive pulse even when the mix leans drum‑heavy on some boards. The highlight is the electric China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider segue, which crackles with intensity, and the tight, high‑energy delivery of Touch of Grey and Far From Me that keeps the audience cruising. Though a few recordings suffer from tinny balance or occasional focus lapses, the Miller clean‑up soundboard capture presents the performance in crisp, clean detail, making this show a must‑listen for fans interested in a pivotal moment in Phil’s career and a solid snapshot of the 1982 Dead.

best_recording.reason: Excellent post‑show cleanup provides crystal‑clear soundboard audio, capturing the historic six‑string bass debut and overall band energy

key_highlights: Electric China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition
Phil Lesh's first performance on an Alembic six‑string bass
Tight, high‑energy delivery of Touch of Grey and Far From Me
Overall 1982 band sound captured cleanly on the Miller SBD

band_performance.Jerry: Articulate lead throughout, especially on “Eyes Of The World,” with powerful guitar tones that keep the band soaring.
band_performance.Phil: Debuts his Alembic six‑string bass, delivering a fuller low end and adding fresh melodic possibilities while holding down the groove.
band_performance.Bob: Provides steady rhythm guitar foundation, complementing Jerry’s leads and keeping the songs grounded.
band_performance.Brent: Adds subtle keyboard textures that enhance the jams without overwhelming the mix, typical of his supportive style in this era.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are prominent on several boards, driving the set with a solid pulse; overall percussion stays tight despite occasional mix bleed.
band_performance.Billy: Keeps a steady backbeat and locks in tightly with Mickey, contributing to the show’s propulsive energy.
